speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. To help me understand your pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities, can you describe how long you have had this rash and if it has changed over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the rash has persisted for five months without resolution and you have no new exposures, have you noticed any specific triggers like heat, sweating, or wearing certain fabrics that seem to worsen the itching? Additionally, does the rash appear in a distinct pattern, such as on the inner elbows or wrists?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (sarcoptic mange).

The chronic, pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities without systemic symptoms or new exposures is highly suggestive of scabies; I am requesting images to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of bilateral upper extremities.
